New features and improvements, newest first

What shipped in Famulor 2.0, newest first. The list starts with the 2.0 launch on August 17, 2026.

MilianAutomationsAssistantsAcademyMissionsToolsTelephonyFlow BuilderAPIHistoryMobile
October 28, 2026

​
Clickable answer buttons in live chat

In website chat and Test Chat, an assistant can now show 2–5 clickable answer buttons under its message when the visitor is choosing among a few known options. Until now, every answer had to be typed.
  • Off until you turn it on: in the assistant’s Settings → Conversation → Live chat → Interactive responses, switch on Quick replies. The When to use them (optional) field tells the assistant when buttons help.
  • A click is a normal message: the visitor can always type instead. Phone calls, web voice, WhatsApp and other messaging, and email ignore the setting. It is not the same as the quick-reply buttons on a WhatsApp template.
  • In History: the conversation shows the tool call as Show quick replies, and a click appears as the visitor’s message.
Quick replies · Interactive responses

​
Separate transfer hours for each transfer

Call transfers now support custom transfer hours. Until now, a transfer tool could connect at any time — the only hours the assistant knew were the general opening hours from the Business hours tool. You can now define separate timeframes for when call transfers are allowed. For example, your business is open from 8 AM to 6 PM, but accounting only takes calls until 3 PM.
  • Set it per tool: turn on Restrict transfer hours on a call transfer or warm call transfer tool and add up to four windows per weekday. Night services such as 18:00–08:00 work too, and each tool can use its own timezone.
  • No dead ends: outside the hours nothing is dialed. The assistant learns when the next transfer is possible and is instructed to tell the caller and to offer to take a message or arrange a callback; the conversation continues. In flows, a refused transfer never ends the call.
  • Nothing changes until you turn it on: existing transfer tools keep transferring at any time.
Each refused transfer is recorded as a call event. Transfer hours are also available through the API (PATCH /api/v1/tools/{id}), MCP (update_tool) and the command line (famulor update-tool).Transfer hours

​
Choose how deeply Milian thinks

A quick question and a full campaign analysis no longer get the same amount of thinking. Milian now has four thinking levels: Low, Medium, High and Extra high.
  • In the composer: the gauge button in the Milian composer opens Thinking level. Drag the slider or use the arrow keys. Medium is the default, and Milian remembers your choice in this browser. This works on the dashboard and in the side panel.
  • For missions: in Mission Studio, the Access tab has a Thinking level select under Limits. Every run of that mission uses it. Default follows the platform default.
  • Credits: higher levels think longer and can use more credits. You pay for actual usage, as before.
Through the Public API and the ask_milian MCP tool, send effort (low, medium, high or xhigh). Missions take the same field in their version spec.Ask Milian through the API

​
Folders, templates and share links for automations

Setting up the same follow-up for every client, or sending a colleague screenshots of your steps? Automations now have folders, a template gallery and share links. Until now, every automation sat in one long list and started from an empty canvas.
  • Folders: choose New → New folder and move automations with Move to folder… in the ⋯ menu, for example one folder per client or location. Deleting a folder never deletes its automations.
  • 41 templates: New → Start from template opens ready-made automations for calls, bookings, leads, messaging, CRM and team alerts. Use template creates a draft and marks every step that still needs your own account, number, assistant or recipient.
  • Share without keys: Share… in the ⋯ menu creates a link. Anyone who opens it sees the steps and can add a copy to their own workspace. Connections, API keys, passwords, phone numbers and assistants never travel with it. Text you typed into steps, such as prompts or email addresses, stays, so check it before you share. Update link shows your latest version under the same link, and Stop sharing turns it off at once.
  • Export and import: Export downloads a .famulor-automation.json file, and Import next to New turns one into a draft, in this or another workspace.
  • On or off from the list: every row has a switch for Live and Paused. An automation goes live only once its required fields are filled in and placeholders such as YOUR_API_KEY are replaced.
  • New connection right there: the Connections tab has its own New connection button.
Booking triggers now also pass flat fields such as invitee_name, invitee_email, invitee_phone, start_at and end_at, so a booking automation can greet the guest by name without digging through nested data.Folders, templates, share links, export and import also work through the API, MCP, the command line (famulor 0.1.12), SDK 0.2.7, the n8n node 2.4.0 and the Famulor Skill 2.4.0. Update your n8n node and the Skill to get the new actions.Folders, templates and sharing

​
Waiting automations no longer hold up new events

An automation that waits in a delay step, for example 30 minutes before a reminder, no longer blocks the next events. Until now, three waiting runs were enough for the next booking or call to be turned away.
  • Waiting isn’t working: up to three runs per automation can still work at the same time, and up to 200 more can wait.
  • Paused stays paused: if you pause, archive or delete an automation while runs are waiting, they stop when they wake up and send nothing. The run history shows them as cancelled.
There’s nothing to set up. A delay still waits at most one day.

​
Transcripts in the order things were said

After an interruption or a handoff to another assistant, a call transcript could list lines in the wrong order. For example, a caller confirms their details, the assistant checks them and hands the call to a second assistant, and that assistant’s first sentence showed up before the caller’s last words, although it was said seconds later. This affected the API, webhooks, automations, the mobile app and some calls in History.
  • One order, everywhere: every line, tool call and tool result is listed at the moment it started. When the caller talks while the assistant is speaking, whatever started first comes first. Typed chats keep the order the messages were sent.
  • Older calls too: calls from before this change get the same order when you open or fetch them. Their content stays the same; only the order is corrected.
  • The same list in every place: History, the mobile app, the API, MCP, webhooks and automations now show a call the same way.
  • One card per tool in History: a tool that reports progress while it runs now appears as one card with its progress steps instead of several cards. Times in History now show when each line or step started, so a few can differ slightly from before.
  • For developers: call transcripts in the API and in webhooks carry order_version: 2, timeline_seq is an item’s position and started_at its start time. Saved Zaps and n8n workflows keep working without changes.
In the mobile app, call transcripts now match History, with a time on every line. Update to version 1.5.4 from the App Store or Google Play to get this.Conversation history · Post-call webhooks

​
QA scorecards: no more 0 % for silent calls, and the judge sees what the assistant did

Until now, a call in which the caller never said a word got 0 % and Failed on its QA scorecard, for example when someone hung up silently right after the greeting. And the QA judge only read what was said: a criterion like “Transfers only during service hours” could score 0, even though the assistant had checked the time with a tool and then transferred the caller.
  • Not scorable instead of 0 %: calls in which the caller never spoke, that never connected, or whose speech couldn’t be transcribed now show Not scorable with the reason. They count neither as passed nor as failed and no longer pull down QA averages, pass rates or the Audience Call QA average.
  • The judge sees actions: tool calls and their results, handoffs, transfers and how the call ended are now part of what the judge reads, in phone calls, web calls, WhatsApp calls and web chat. The caller never hears these lines.
  • Criteria that don’t apply: the judge can mark a criterion Not applicable, for example a callback criterion in a call that was transferred right away. It is left out of the overall score instead of counting as 0.
  • Outages stay visible: if the QA judge fails, the call shows QA judge unavailable instead of a silent 0 %.
  • Find these calls: they no longer appear under QA result → Failed. Filter History by QA result → Not scorable, or use GET /api/v1/history?qa=not_scorable, the MCP tool list_history or famulor list-history --qa not_scorable.
Scores can change from today: criteria that depend on actions, such as transfers, bookings or checks, may now score higher, because the judge sees that the assistant carried them out. In the API, MCP and webhooks, qa_scorecard now has status and reason, and score and passed are null when a call wasn’t scored. If an automation branches on passed, treat null as “no result”.In AI Quality Assurance cohorts, calls without caller speech are listed as No caller speech: they are not judged, not charged and not counted in totals or averages.AI QA scorecards · AI Quality Assurance

October 27, 2026

​
Cal.com bookings in your caller’s language, at the place they choose

When an assistant books through Cal.com, your guest’s confirmation email now arrives in the language of the conversation. Until now, Cal.com sent it in English, even when the assistant spoke German or French.
  • Right language: the email follows the language the assistant speaks in the call or chat, otherwise its primary language. There’s nothing to set up.
  • Right place: if your event type offers several locations, for example Google Meet and a phone call, the assistant books the one the caller asks for. Without a preference, Cal.com’s default location applies as before.
  • Ask first, if you want: turn on Ask callers which location they prefer under Meeting location in the Cal.com integration. When the event type offers at least two locations, the assistant then asks before booking, unless the caller already said where; without a preference it books the default.
  • Always current: the locations come straight from your Cal.com event type. Change them in Cal.com and the next conversation uses them, without editing the integration.
This works on phone and web calls, WhatsApp calls, web chat, messaging channels and email.Calendar booking

​
Announced transfers go through, exactly once

When an assistant tells a caller it is connecting them, the transfer now really follows, and only once. Until now, an assistant could announce a transfer without starting it, or start it a second time after the caller was already through.
  • Announced means started: if the assistant says “I’m connecting you now” but doesn’t start the transfer, Famulor starts it right away. Announced texts, emails and hang-ups work the same way. A check beforehand, for example of the time against your service hours, no longer gets in the way.
  • Offers stay offers: “If you like, I can connect you with a colleague” leaves the choice to the caller and starts nothing.
  • Quiet after the transfer: once a transfer has gone through, the assistant says nothing more and never transfers a second time, on every transfer path, including fallbacks and transfer nodes in flows.
There’s nothing to set up. Announcements are recognized in German and English conversations.Built-in tools

Plans and lists on your phone

Page actions that wrap under the title stay on the right, list rows show full names and numbers, (i) icons are easier to tap, and the Live monitoring button on a running call fits again.

​
Your assistant, in more places

The same assistant can now answer in ten more places: Linear, Notion, Mattermost, Webex, Lark / Feishu, LINE, Twitch, Sendblue, Linq and Zernio.
  • Connect a place: open Settings → Channels, choose the channel and follow its setup guide. The channel is available when your plan includes it.
  • Stay in the thread: when someone @mentions the assistant in Slack, Teams, Discord, Google Chat, Linear, Notion, Twitch, Mattermost, Webex or Lark, later replies in that same thread still reach the assistant.
  • Reply from History: Instagram and Messenger stay inside the 24-hour reply window. In Mattermost, Webex, Linq and Notion you can send one file back in the thread, up to 3 MB.
Each new channel, and the channels you already use, has its own guide: what it is, why an assistant belongs there, and how to connect it.Open Channels · Set up Linear · Set up LINE

​
Duplicate an automation instead of rebuilding it

Need the same follow-up flow for a second customer or location? Choose Duplicate in the automation list or in the editor. Until now, you had to rebuild every step by hand.
  • Everything comes along: the copy is called “Name (Copy)” and keeps every step, trigger, setting, tag and the error notification.
  • Starts as a draft: the copy stays off until you turn it on, so a live automation never runs twice.
  • Its own connections: inbound webhooks get a new secret, and the copy gets its own app-event subscription when you turn it on. If an assistant should start the copy, connect it yourself. When the original runs after an assistant’s calls, keep the copy as a draft until you decide which one stays connected.
Duplicating also works through the API (POST /api/v1/automations/{id}/duplicate), MCP (duplicate_automation), the command line (famulor duplicate-automation) and SDK 0.2.6.Automations overview

New credit rates for messages and email

From October 24, messages in WhatsApp and messaging channels, workspace emails and web chat use new base credit rates. Calls, SMS and all other rates stay the same.Your workspace’s own rates are always listed under Usage → How credits are calculated and in Settings → Balance → How billing works. Both now show every rate for voice, avatars, WhatsApp, messaging channels, web chat, email and SMS, and name the channels each rate covers. On Usage, Credits by channel now also breaks each category down by channel.How usage is billed

​
Your MCP servers, on every call

You connected an MCP server, for example from HubSpot or Salesforce, and Load tools worked, but in calls the assistant didn’t use those tools? Some servers whose address doesn’t end in /mcp were left out when a call started, and the call went on without them. They now connect on phone calls, web calls, web chat and WhatsApp calls.
  • Clear token errors: when a server rejects your token, Load tools now says Token rejected or expired and tells you what to do next. Before, it looked like the server couldn’t be reached.
  • Short-lived tokens: some providers, such as Salesforce, issue access tokens that expire after a few hours. If tools stop loading, paste a new token.
Agent Tools

More HighLevel and Close options

Agencies can now find three more connectors in the app marketplace under Automations → Connections: HighLevel Location with more than 550 actions, HighLevel MCP and Close MCP. They sit next to the native HighLevel and Close integrations, which stay as they are.

For partners: managed plans and reseller billing

  • Managed plans renew or end clearly: Auto top-up, then renew is preselected and recommended when auto top-up with a saved card is on. If a renewal is still unfunded three days after the funded period ends, the managed plan ends: unused funded credits return to your balance and the customer moves to your free plan. The dialog shows Renewal pending or Ending with the date and the missing credits.
  • Plan changes charge the right fee: upgrades and add-ons added mid-period on resold subscriptions now collect the full platform fee up front. A change that can’t be charged correctly is refused before anything is billed. Before, a paid change could leave the customer workspace past due.
  • Credits stay covered: a credit transfer can’t move credits that running calls have reserved.
  • Clearer numbers: the plan limit for own numbers is now called Verified own numbers (caller ID). Plan-included free phone numbers are not available to white-label customers. Phone numbers and SMS registrations are not part of a managed plan.
  • Lighter plan editor: explanations sit in (i) tooltips, each pricing problem shows under its field, and one bar splits the plan price into platform fee, payment reserve and your share.
  • Your brand during outages: if your custom domain can’t load its branding, visitors see a neutral maintenance screen instead of Famulor branding.
Managed customer plans

​
Hand a chat or email to the right assistant

Transfer to another assistant used to work only on calls and in web chat. Now it also works in WhatsApp, SMS, Instagram, Slack, connected mailboxes and every other messaging channel, and in assistant email. For example, your support assistant hands an invoice question to your billing assistant, and the customer gets the answer in the same thread.
  • Same thread, own setup: the receiving assistant answers in the same reply, with its own instructions, knowledge and tools, and keeps answering the customer’s next messages. The channel’s default assistant doesn’t change.
  • You decide what it knows: choose the same context as on calls: the full history, a summary plus the last messages (recommended), only the last messages, a summary or a clean start. A message before the handoff and the target’s greeting are optional.
  • Safe handoffs: actions the first assistant started finish before the handoff. Human takeover, recipient checks and the protection against duplicate emails and texts still apply.
Transfer to another assistant

Magicline Connect: book trial sessions in the conversation

“Can I try a class on Friday?” Your assistant can now book the trial session itself. The new Magicline Connect API connector finds your studios, checks free times and books once the visitor has confirmed. You don’t need a Magicline API key. The existing connector is now called Magicline Open API and keeps reading studio and course data.
  • Find your studios: open Agent Tools → Marketplace → Magicline Connect API, enter your Connect API URL and choose Load studios. Search by name or city and pick one studio or All studios in this account. Studio IDs are filled in for you.
  • Book only after a yes: the assistant confirms the studio, reads the required fields and free times, collects the details and asks the visitor to confirm before it books. It says “booked” only after Magicline confirms. Repeated or parallel requests don’t create double bookings.
  • Trainer preference: choose Studio default, With a trainer or Without a trainer, if your studio allows it. A specific trainer can’t be picked.
  • In automations too: connect Magicline Connect API under Automations → Connections and use its requirements, free times and booking actions.
Your studio needs Connect API enabled, and online trial sessions for bookings. Free times are not reservations: if a time fills up, the assistant loads new times. Setup also works through the API, MCP and the command line.Set up Magicline Connect · Magicline Open API

Grok Voice 3.0: a new voice for your assistants

Your assistant can now hold spoken conversations with Grok Voice 3.0. Native speech-to-speech brings listening and expressive speech into one conversation model, with 28 public voices to choose from.
  • Choose your voice: open Assistant settings → General → Realtime → Standard, select Grok Voice 3.0, then choose a compatible voice. Eve is the recommended starting point; Rex and Ara are other options. Preview a voice before saving.
  • Connect the next step: use your assistant’s assigned tools to look up information or continue a workflow during the conversation. Follow the same tool permissions and configuration as your other assistants.
  • Make it useful: try customer questions, appointment intake, language practice or initial sales conversations. Test the assistant with your own prompts, tools and callers.
Manual model selection requires AI Safety & Control. Grok Voice is available in Global and US workspaces and has no dedicated EU endpoint. Use Realtime → Standard; Half-Cascade and Full Duplex are separate engine choices.
A Famulor voice agent running on Grok Voice 3.0.Choose models and voices · Check AI regions

​
Signed webhooks for your own apps

Send call, conversation and booking events straight to your own HTTPS receiver. A workspace owner or admin registers the receiver and picks its events: call.completed, conversation.ended, booking.created, booking.cancelled and booking.rescheduled.
  • Signed deliveries: every event is signed with HMAC-SHA256 in the X-Famulor-Signature header. Your signing secret stays with your receiver and is never shown again.
  • Wherever you build: create, list and delete subscriptions through the API, MCP, the command line and the SDK.
  • n8n sets itself up: with n8n-nodes-famulor 2.3.0 or later, a new Famulor Trigger registers its subscription when you activate the workflow and removes it when you deactivate it. Existing workflows keep their manual setup. Update the package in n8n to use it.
  • Zapier templates: the Zapier page now shows ready-made Zap templates you can start from.
Set up webhook subscriptions · n8n · Zapier

Magicline: your studio, in the conversation

“Which classes are on tomorrow?” “Is there still a place?” Your assistant can now look up studio information, courses and availability through Magicline, while the visitor stays in the conversation.Connect your studio under Agent Tools → Marketplace → Magicline, enter its Studio ID, API key and Magicline Open API URL, then assign the connection to an assistant. Greet website visitors before they click

Your website widget can now say hello first. Under Appearance → Launcher, turn on Greeting bubble. Your greeting then appears next to the closed launcher when a visitor hovers over it or reaches it with the keyboard, and a click on the bubble opens the widget.
  • Show it on its own: under Also show automatically, choose Desktop, Mobile or both, and set how many seconds (0–60) after loading the bubble appears. It shows at most once per browser tab, waits while the tab is in the background and stays hidden once the visitor has opened the widget.
  • Write once, greet in every language: under Messages → Chat, write your Greeting message, pick the language you wrote it in and keep Auto-translate on. When you save, the headline and greeting are translated into your assistant’s languages, up to 40. Visitors see them in their browser language, or in the assistant’s main language.
  • Stay in control: the editor shows which languages are translated, and Retry translation fills in any that are missing. New widgets start with Auto-translate on. Existing widgets keep their greeting as it is until you turn it on.
The greeting bubble works with the classic floating launcher. Inline widgets and full-screen avatar widgets don’t show it.Set up the greeting bubble · Translate your greeting

New app integration: Personio

Connect Personio to Automations and use your HR data in workflows: people, employments, absences, attendances, time-tracking projects and documents. For example, check who is absent today, or pull a person’s employment details into a follow-up workflow.Personio has no sign-in window for other apps, so you connect it with your own Personio API credential. Create the credential in Personio under Marketplace → Connected integrations → API credentials with read access to persons. Then open Automations → Connections → App marketplace → Personio and paste its Client ID and secret. Famulor checks the credential right away. It stays at the app connector and is never stored in your workspace.
  • Ten read actions: list persons, employments, absence periods and types, attendance periods, projects, documents and document categories, employee attributes and employee records.
  • Replace credentials any time: edit the connection and paste a new pair. The old credential is removed in the same step.
  • Milian knows the way: ask Milian to connect Personio and it points you to the form, because credentials never go into the chat.
Connect Personio

​
Emails and texts that reach the right person, once

When your assistant sends an email or a text message during a chat, an email conversation or a call, it now makes sure the recipient is right, and it sends each message only once.
  • Confirmed email recipients: with Ask on the call as the recipient, the assistant asks for the address or reads back the one it knows, and sends only after the customer confirms it. In chats, the address must come from the customer, never from a web page or a tool result.
  • Texts to the right number: in SMS and WhatsApp chats, texts always go to the chat’s own number. In other chats, the assistant only texts a number the customer wrote.
  • No duplicates: if a chat or email reply is generated again, an email or text that already went out is not sent a second time. When the customer asks for it again, it goes out again.
  • Numbers as people write them: texts and callbacks accept numbers such as +49 176 …, 0049 … or WhatsApp numbers without a plus. When a number has no country code, the assistant asks for it instead of guessing.
  • No gaps in your emails: placeholders in custom email signatures, such as the assistant’s name, are filled in. If a required value is missing, the email is not sent.
  • Calls stay on track: calls no longer go silent when the AI model sends a malformed tool request, for example while asking for an email address. Confirming a collected email address, name or phone number now works on the first “yes” with Realtime, Half-Cascade and Full Duplex too.
How the SMS and email tools work

​
Give your assistant a browser

Your assistant can now work with approved websites during a conversation. Create a Browser Use tool in Agent Tools, choose a starting page and allowed websites, and assign it to an assistant. Use it to look up information or complete supported website steps with the details provided in the conversation.
  • Start with practical lookups: Compare visible flight fares on Google Flights, hotel prices, appointment availability, product stock or shipment status. The guide includes starting pages, required information and example browser instructions. Test the selected website flow before using it with customers.
  • Configure the task once: Save Browser instructions and Required information directly in the tool, then assign it to an assistant. The assistant asks for missing information before opening the browser; the main assistant prompt does not need to repeat the browser steps.
  • See the task live: Open View browser in Test Call or Test Chat. The side drawer opens automatically when the assistant starts a browser task. Enabled public demos offer the same live view.
  • Replay what happened: When a browser video is available, the browser recording icon in History opens a video player. Recordings are private to the workspace and follow its retention settings, up to seven days.
  • Control access and usage: Browser Use is available to Famulor workspaces on enabled plans, including a whitelabel reseller’s own workspace. Browser tasks use separate credits, shown as Browser Use in usage history. Reseller customer workspaces are not included yet.
Phone, website-widget and WhatsApp conversations keep their familiar interface. The browser tool runs when the assistant needs it; the live viewer is for testing and enabled public demos.Set up Browser Use

Learn, build and get certified with Famulor Academy

Build your first AI agent or sharpen your team’s skills with the new Famulor Academy. Eight courses and 31 interactive lessons combine animations, practical exercises and a mascot coach with hints. Open Academy in the sidebar of your own Famulor workspace.
  • Start with the basics: AI Voice Agent Foundations guides you through prompts, greetings, voices, knowledge and tools to testing and launching an agent. Famulor Grand Tour helps you find your way around numbers, campaigns, monitoring and usage.

  • One conversation view: Read incoming messages, AI replies and manual replies in History → SMS, with delivery status and charged credits.
  • Reply yourself: Type directly in the conversation, just like chat. Sending a manual reply pauses AI for that conversation; resume it when ready. SMS replies are text only, with no file attachments.
  • Keep it to one SMS: The composer counts up to 160 GSM-7 units or 70 Unicode units. Special characters can use more than one unit. Overlong replies cannot be sent, and assistant replies stay within the same limit.
  • Simple setup: Twilio imports have an optional Enable SMS conversations checkbox, off by default. Eligible numbers show the same registration badge as Phone numbers; click it to open that number’s registration form.
SMS uses your existing SMS credit rate, with applicable carrier charges and no extra general chat-message fee. Number and destination eligibility, registration requirements, consent and workspace limits still apply.Set up SMS conversations

October 2, 2026

​
Show your screen, get better help

​
Screen sharing in web widgets

Visitors can now share a screen, window or browser tab with your AI assistant during chat or voice conversations. Enable General → Screen sharing in the widget editor, then visitors choose what to share in their browser using the screen icon next to the microphone or paperclip. The feature is off by default and requires a workspace plan with Web widgets.Sharing requires the visitor’s explicit selection and can be stopped with the same icon. Closing the widget, changing its tab or ending the session also stops sharing. Use a supported desktop browser on HTTPS; phones do not show the icon. The assistant can explain visible content, but cannot click or control the device. System and tab audio are not shared, and screenshots are processed on demand without being saved as attachments.Configure widget screen sharing

​
Fresher screen help and simpler Milian controls (Beta)

Milian now requests a current view whenever a question needs the shared screen, helping it follow changes in the screen or window you selected. Voice mode keeps a compact input row and toolbar: page context, screen sharing and microphone controls are icon toggles. The eye icon pauses or resumes page context and dims while screen sharing is active. New voice messages also arrive without a flashing scrollbar. Enable Beta Features in your workspace to use Milian voice.Learn about Milian voice and screen help

​
What you can use it for

  • Customer support: Visitors can show an error message or the step where they are stuck. The assistant can explain what is visible and suggest the next step.
  • Onboarding: New users can share a setup page and ask where to find a setting or how to complete a step, without describing the whole screen.
  • Shopping assistance: Customers can show a product page or comparison table and ask the assistant to explain the visible options, alongside information from your knowledge base.
  • Booking help: Visitors can share a booking page and ask for help understanding the available dates or completing the next step themselves.
  • Workspace guidance with Milian (Beta): Share your assistant settings, flow editor or dashboard and ask Milian to explain the visible configuration or help you find the relevant controls.

KnowledgeAPICLI
October 1, 2026

​
Better answers from your website

Website imports now keep the content your assistants need and leave out what gets in the way.
  • No more cookie banners or menus in your knowledge base. Consent banners and dialogs, navigation and footers are removed before a page is indexed; prices, opening hours, allergens and other details stay.
  • Every passage knows where it belongs. Pages are split along their headings, and each passage starts with the page title and section name, for example Pizza Hawaii › Ingredients. Assistants find the ingredient list, allergens or baking time of the right product instead of a similar one.
  • Less noise. Error pages, pages without readable content and pages with identical content are skipped and use no credits. An error page never replaces a page that was indexed before.
Existing website sources pick up the new cleaning at their next refresh. This one-time re-index is free. Pages imported earlier that are now skipped stay in your knowledge base until you delete them.

​
The same structure for files and texts

PDFs, Word files, Markdown and text files, typed text and HTML files are now prepared like websites:
  • Every passage starts with the document name, so even a passage from the middle of a catalog says which document it comes from.
  • Word and Markdown headings split a document into sections, for example Speisekarte › Pizza Hawaii › Zutaten.
  • PDF page numbers disappear, and headers or footers that repeat on almost every page are kept only once.
  • HTML files lose their cookie banners, like websites.
Documents already in your knowledge bases are converted once automatically, free of charge.How content is prepared

​
Choose exactly which pages to import

  • Tick individual pages in the page preview. Each checkbox adds an entry for exactly that page (ending in $, for example /impressum$); a path without $ still covers every page below it.
  • The page limit follows your selection. Maximum pages rises automatically so every include path and ticked page fits, and you can type an exact number. The dialog and the Auto Refresh cards warn you when a source has more include paths than its page limit.
  • Refresh less often when content rarely changes. Auto Refresh for websites and auto-sync for cloud drives now run from every 6 hours up to every 6 months.
  • Privacy, cookie and accessibility pages are suggested as exclusions; the imprint and terms are never suggested.
Import a website

​
Delete several documents at once

Hover over a document and tick its checkbox, then use Select all or Delete selected in the bar above the list. Deleting also removes the indexed passages, so assistants stop using that content right away.
  • API: DELETE /knowledge-bases/{id}/documents/{docId} for one document, POST /knowledge-bases/{id}/documents/delete for up to 200
  • MCP: delete_documents
  • CLI: famulor delete-knowledge-base-document and famulor delete-knowledge-base-documents
Delete documents

The Famulor CLI

Available as a public preview. Requires Node.js 22 or newer and a workspace plan with API Access. Command names may change before version 1.0.Your whole Famulor workspace is now available in the terminal. Every REST API operation is a command: create assistants, start calls, run campaigns, manage leads and phone numbers, and read call history, all from one tool.
npm install --global famulor
famulor auth login
famulor list-assistants --output table
  • Log in once with an API key from Settings → API & MCP. The key is stored in your system keychain, with one profile per workspace and support for white-label domains.
  • Tables, JSON or JSON Lines, with --all to fetch every page of a list.
  • Safe for scripts and CI: deletes and irreversible actions need confirmation, --dry-run shows a request before it is sent, rate limits are retried automatically, and in scripts a failure ends with one JSON error line on stderr.
  • Made for coding agents: famulor commands <topic> finds the right command and famulor <command> --help --output json describes it, so Claude Code, Codex or Cursor can use Famulor directly.

Automatic retries for warm transfers

Keep trying the same team member when a warm transfer reaches no answer, a busy line, temporary unavailability or detected voicemail. The caller stays connected while the assistant retries automatically — useful for on-call teams and 24/7 support.

A calendar view for your appointments

Booking now offers a month, week and day calendar next to the familiar list.

Click, drag, and it’s booked

The calendar view gets a Google Calendar-style header and sidebar, live updates, and the ability to book and move appointments yourself, right from the grid.

  • API and MCP parity. POST /api/v1/bookings, POST /api/v1/bookings/{id}/reschedule and their MCP equivalents (create_booking, reschedule_booking, plus the new get_booking_slots) support the same staff override via allow_outside_availability.

Milian now has a memory

Milian remembers what matters across chats — your business, your preferences, house rules — so you don’t repeat yourself in every conversation. Memory has two scopes: personal (your language, role, how you like to work) and shared workspace facts (company, industry, hours, tone) that every team member’s Milian knows.
  • Only the important things — Milian keeps stable facts you state or confirm, never one-off task details, phone numbers, secrets, or caller data. Facts expire 180 days after they were last confirmed.
  • Search and reference chats — Milian can look up details from your own earlier chats when you say “like we discussed yesterday”.
  • Generate memory from chats — after a conversation, Milian distils durable facts automatically. Both switches, plus everything Milian remembers, live under Settings → Milian where you can delete single facts or clear them all.

​
More expressive multilingual voices

The voice library now includes more multilingual voices that can keep a consistent identity when the conversation changes language. Choose a voice compatible with your assistant’s configured languages.
  • Audio tags for delivery — supported voices can use tags such as [whispering], [laughing], or [excited] to guide how a response is spoken.
  • Regional speech processing — these speech-recognition and voice-generation options follow your workspace’s EU or US AI region setting.
  • Preview available voices directly in the voice library before choosing one.

​
Force a tool call — so the AI never skips the step that matters

Some steps in a flow shouldn’t be optional. A new Force tool call toggle on any tool node in Flow Builder guarantees the assistant actually calls that tool — booking the appointment, checking availability, whatever it is — instead of talking past it. Built-in safeguards mean a call can never get stuck: after a few failed attempts, the assistant gracefully continues the conversation instead of looping forever.

​
Check before you save

Flow Builder now catches problems before they reach a live caller. If a tool node is missing its tool, or the greeting has gotten too long, saving shows a clear Check before saving summary — fix it, or save anyway if you know what you’re doing.Save failures are also easier to spot: instead of a small red line you could miss, a dialog now tells you exactly what went wrong.

​
Public demo links can now expire

Sharing a live demo of an assistant? Set the link to expire in 2 hours, 24 hours, 1 week, or 30 days — perfect for a trade show, a sales call, or a time-boxed trial. The demo panel shows a live countdown, and hovering reveals the exact expiry time in your workspace’s timezone.

​
Cleaner call details

Call History detail pages got tidier: Usage & Cost and Webhook & Automation now collapse by default (your preference is remembered), and latency and action labels reveal themselves on hover instead of crowding the view — especially nice on smaller screens.
​
AssistantsAutomation
August 30, 2026

​
Turn recurring work into event-driven Missions

Milian Missions now include Mission Studio: one place to define what should happen, what starts the work, which workspace context Milian may use, and which actions it may take. Existing manual and scheduled Missions continue to work, while event-driven Missions can start as soon as something changes in your workspace.
  • Add context as you type — enter @ to insert an assistant, automation, Mission, call, contact, campaign, knowledge base, segment, booking, phone number, saved app connection, or active Agent Tool. Each selection becomes a clear chip with its icon or avatar. Enter / for Milian actions and skills.
  • Start from the event that matters — in addition to manual and scheduled runs, a Mission can react to completed calls, conversations, messages and incoming email, bookings, new leads, inbound webhooks, CRM events, and events from a connected app. Event triggers are available when Workspace Beta Features are enabled; classic manual and scheduled Missions remain available without them.
  • Publish with clear boundaries — review the objective, trigger, filters, referenced resources, app connections, allowed actions, and run limits before activation. A published version stays unchanged; later edits become a new draft and do not alter work already running.
  • Understand every run — Mission Studio shows the active version, last and next run, status, credit usage, attention state, and transcript. Events wait in order when a Mission is already running, so they are not silently dropped.

​
More choice for clear pronunciation

New voice options help assistants pronounce names, addresses and numbers clearly. Preview them in the voice library to choose the delivery that fits your business.Some voices support a single language. For an assistant with additional languages, choose a compatible multilingual voice; the voice picker accounts for your assistant’s language configuration.
​
AssistantsTelephony
August 29, 2026

​
Warm transfers can bring a message back to the caller

A warm transfer no longer leaves the assistant guessing when the handoff doesn’t complete. If the supervisor answers but cannot take the call, they can say, for example, “Ask them to call back in an hour” and hang up. The assistant returns to the caller, briefly relays the relevant message in the caller’s language, and continues the conversation.
  • The outcome is always shared — the assistant receives the classified reason: busy, declined, no answer, or temporarily unavailable. It is explicitly told never to invent something the supervisor did not say.
  • Consultation notes are your choice — Share supervisor conversation with the AI (consultation notes) controls whether the assistant sees the supervisor-side conversation when the supervisor actually spoke. The transcript is always saved to the call record, even when sharing is off. If nobody answers, there are no consultation notes — only the outcome.
  • Every warm-transfer path behaves consistently — this works in Flow Builder warm transfers, the Warm transfer tool, and Famulor Loop Recall. Consultation notes are always enabled for Loop Recall because there is no separate transfer form there.

Create AI-native automations and run them during a conversation

Create AI-native automations in Famulor, connect them to an assistant, and run them while the conversation is still going.The assistant can start a workflow during a phone call, web chat, messaging conversation, or email. You decide when it should run and which information it passes into the workflow.Capture leads, submit callback requests, create tasks, and run other business processes from the conversation itself.

Faster conversational voice responses

Milian offers to top up your credit, right in the chat

Assign a tool to several assistants at once

Select Assign on any tool in Agent Tools to see and change which assistants use it — search the list, tick the ones you want, save. No more opening each assistant to add the same tool one at a time.

​
Assistants can call an automation mid-conversation

An assistant can now trigger an automation while it’s still talking to someone, not only after the conversation ends. Describe in plain language when it should run, switch that automation to Live, and the assistant decides in the moment to use it — across voice, web chat, messaging, and email.

​
Assistants can look up current information on the web

A new Perplexity research connector in Agent Connectors lets an assistant fetch up-to-date answers during a call or a chat, beyond what’s already in its knowledge base. Install it with your own Perplexity API key, pick the model your account offers, and optionally set a system prompt for tone, language, and answer format — then assign the tool to as many assistants as you like.

​
Workspace-scoped API keys

Issue a Public API key scoped to a single workspace, with its own permissions and expiry, instead of only account-wide keys.

​
Start from a ready-made assistant, not a blank page

The Create assistant gallery now includes complete flow blueprints for common use cases, not just prompt templates. Each one shows what it’s built to do, which surfaces it works on, and anything you still need to finish before it goes live. See Start from a use-case template.

​
Teach an assistant your key terms

Add up to 100 product names, brand terms, and other key vocabulary so speech recognition transcribes them correctly. Open Assistant settings → Voice → Speech recognition to build the glossary — it’s a plan feature, and the settings appear only for the engine modes and speech-recognition providers that support it. An optional Detect key terms automatically (Beta) toggle can pick up further terms for the current call.

​
Ten new inboxes your assistant can answer in (Beta)

Freshdesk, Gmail, Outlook, Zendesk, ServiceNow, Intercom, Zoho Mail, AgentMail, Instagram, and Zulip join WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, and the rest of messaging — sign in to the account once and your assistant reads and replies automatically. Gmail and Outlook can watch the Inbox, the whole mailbox, or a single label or folder, and either send replies straight away or leave a draft for you to review. Turn on Beta Features under Settings → Workspace to see them.

​
Three more ways to keep your knowledge base current (Beta)

Sync a knowledge base from Box, Dropbox, or SharePoint now too, alongside the existing Google Drive and OneDrive sources — kept up to date automatically, the same way a website source is. Cloud drive sync is Beta and carries its own plan feature.

​
Automations can now react to every message, not just the first

An automation triggered by an inbound message used to fire only on the first one. It can now trigger on every inbound message, so a workflow can keep responding as the conversation continues.

​
Milian is now AI-native

Milian, the workspace copilot, can now do more than answer questions — it analyzes your assistants and calls, connects accounts and data sources, builds automations from scratch, and tests them before anything goes live. Most of what you used to click through by hand in the dashboard, you can now just ask Milian to do in chat.

​
Missions — recurring tasks in the background

Milian Missions are scheduled tasks Milian runs for you on a recurring schedule or on demand, with no browser tab required to stay open. New Missions entry in the sidebar.

Rate Milian’s answers

Hover over any Milian response to rate it with a thumbs up or down. After a helpful interaction, Milian may also nudge you to leave Famulor a review.

Test with a real phone call, not just text

Simulation tests can now run as an actual voice call, not only a text conversation. A simulated caller — with its own voice from the voice library — calls your live, unmodified assistant, so you hear exactly what a real customer would experience before you ship a change. Two test modes: fast, text-based Chat, or full audio round-trip Voice. Every test now also scores turn-by-turn response latency and whether the assistant called the tools it was supposed to.

​
Workspace Audit Log — see who changed what

Team accounts can now open Settings → Data → Audit Log for a complete history of changes across the workspace: who changed what, and when, down to the exact field. Searchable, sortable, and paginated.

Multiple workspaces per account

You can now create more than one workspace under a single account — useful for keeping separate brands, clients, or departments cleanly apart without juggling logins. Availability depends on your plan.

After a public beta, Famulor 2.0 is now live for everyone — a rebuilt platform with a faster, cleaner interface, and more capabilities landing since (see above).
